title: Standard PCR amplification
summary: Amplify a defined DNA region from a template using a thermostable polymerase. Foundational protocol — every nucleic-acid workflow assumes you can do this cleanly.

reagents.name: 2× polymerase master mix (Q5, Phusion, or equivalent)

hazardsMd: Standard low-risk reagents. Use gloves to prevent contaminating reactions with skin nucleases.
contentUndergrad:
## What this protocol does
Polymerase chain reaction copies a target DNA region millions of times by repeatedly denaturing, annealing primers, and extending from the primer ends. The annealing temperature you pick is the most common variable to tune.

steps.title: Plan the reaction
steps.instructionMd:
Per 25 μL reaction:
- 12.5 μL 2× master mix
- 1.25 μL forward primer (10 μM → 0.5 μM final)
- 1.25 μL reverse primer
- 1 μL template (1-100 ng)
- 9 μL nuclease-free water

Set annealing temp ~3 °C below your primer's lowest Tm.
steps.verificationMd: Reaction calculator shows totals matching pipetting volumes. Annealing temp written on the tube cap.

steps.title: Set up reactions on ice
steps.instructionMd: Thaw master mix and primers on ice. Vortex briefly + spin down. Make a master mix for n+1 reactions in a single tube. Aliquot into PCR tubes, then add template last.
steps.safetyNotesMd: Always add template last to minimize cross-contamination from earlier pipetting.
steps.verificationMd: All reactions have the same milky-white appearance and identical volume in the well. Template tubes are visibly closed before the next is opened.

steps.title: Run the thermal cycler
steps.instructionMd: Standard program: 98 °C / 30 s → 30× (98 °C / 10 s, Ta °C / 30 s, 72 °C / 30 s per kb) → 72 °C / 5 min → hold 4 °C. Use the heated lid (105 °C).
steps.verificationMd: Cycler shows the program, time-to-completion, and lid icon. Tubes seated firmly in the block; wells around them are filled or capped to maintain heat distribution.

steps.title: Verify by gel
steps.instructionMd: Run 5 μL on a 1-1.5% agarose gel against a molecular-weight ladder. Look for a single sharp band at the expected size.
steps.verificationMd: Single band at the expected size; no smearing; no primer-dimer cloud at the bottom of the lane.

steps.title: Clean up reactions
steps.instructionMd: If passing forward to cloning or sequencing, purify with a PCR cleanup kit. Otherwise, store reactions at −20 °C until needed.
steps.verificationMd: Tubes labeled with date + reaction id. Cleanup column eluted into nuclease-free water (not TE) if downstream is enzymatic.
